description: Rich text cases shared by every HotLayout reader (schema 9.6.0): parts of one string drawn with their own style. A row of `cases` is the two props of a Text node a reader needs (`content`: a `literal`, a `binding` or a `template`; `spans`: the value of `Text.spans`, absent when the node has none) and everything it takes to turn `content` into text, in the same fields as contract/fixtures/template/template-cases.json: `sourceLocale` is `localization.defaultLocale`, `translationLocale` is the `translation` answer of locale resolution, `formattingLocale` is its `formatting` answer, `translations` holds the entries of `localization.strings[translationLocale]` for this value keyed by the path INSIDE the value (`template`, `values.<name>.forms.<category>`, `values.<name>.text`), `data` maps data paths to values (a missing key and null are both `no data`), `now` is the reader clock. The reader must produce `expected` exactly: `text` is the whole string, character for character, and is the string a screen reader hears as ONE node; `runs` are its pieces in LOGICAL order (the order of the shown string, never the visual order of a right-to-left line), each with `span`: the name of the place whose style it is drawn with, or null for the style of the node; empty pieces are dropped and neighbours with the same `span` are merged, so the number of runs is part of the answer; `styles` is what the reader has read from `spans` for the places `content` declares: the styles that apply, field by field. The line pitch of the paragraph is computed over the base style and every name in `styles`, whether the shown string mentions it or not. `direction` is informative: the paragraph direction is that of `directionLocale` (contract/fixtures/locale/locale-cases.json), and a style never isolates or reorders its part. `readerOnly` marks a row with a value the builder cannot produce (the validator or the schema rejects it): it is a rule for readers that meet a document from another producer or a newer minor. U+00A0 is written as an escape. A row of `struts` is the rule of the line: `base` and `spans` are resolved metrics (`fontSize` in logical pixels, `lineHeight` as a multiplier of it) of the text style and of the parts in `styles`; `expected.lineBlock` is the pitch of EVERY line of the paragraph in logical pixels before the system font scale, `expected.span` is the strut: the part whose style places the baseline, null for the text style. Data: `x-style.layout.richText`.

emphasisNote: Schema 9.17.0 — emphasis of text: «style.fontStyle» and «style.textDecoration» of a node, and «weight», «fontStyle», «textDecoration» of a part («Text.spans»). Rules: x-style.layout.textEmphasis. A row of «emphasis» is a row of «cases» plus the emphasis around the text: «inherited» is what the nearest ancestors named (absent — nothing, the root is normal / none), «style» is the two fields of the «style» of the Text node itself, raw. «expected.runs» are the runs of «cases» (the same merging — by place, not by look) with the emphasis each run is drawn with: «fontStyle», «textDecoration», and «weight» — the NUMBER of the weight word the part named, or null when the font style of the run gives the weight. The line of a run has the colour of that run. A row of «emphasisStruts» is a row of «struts» plus «emphasis» (the emphasis fields of each part) and «style» (of the node): the strut is the one the metrics alone give — slant, line and weight never change it.

amountPartsNote: Schema 9.19.0 — parts of a formatted number: «Text.spans[place].parts» («fraction», «currency»; rules: x-money.parts). A row of «amountPartCases» is a row of «cases» with «direction» (the direction of the shown text, as in «moneyCases» of the template table) and with «part» in every expected run: the part whose OWN style the run is drawn with, or null — the style of the place (or of the node, when «span» is null). A part the place gives no style to is not a run of its own: it merges with its neighbours of the same place. «styles» is what the reader has read from «spans», «parts» included. A row of «amountPartStruts» is a row of «struts»: a declared part enters the strut under the key «place.part», with the metric of its style laid over the style of the place.

amountPartCases.mayDiffer: Digits and separators come from the CLDR data of the platform (plain `ar` gives Latin digits on some CLDR versions and Arabic-Indic on others). The sign, the order, the currency sign, the gap and the two isolation marks are fixed.

textGradientNote: Schema 9.23.0 — a gradient on the glyphs of a text: «style.textGradient» (rules: x-textGradient). A gradient token of the theme or an own gradient of the same form as a gradient «background». It lies over the whole content box of the text, one transition for every line; «color» stays the fallback. `textGradientCases`: «type» is the widget, «style» its base style, «styleWhen» its states, «met» which state conditions hold, «parent» the style of the parent (the field is NOT inherited); «gradient» is what paints the letters (null — the colour). `textGradientPartCases`: «spans» the styles of the places of a composed text; «parts» says, place by place, whether its pieces take the gradient (a place that names its own colour keeps it). `textGradientDocumentCases`: «codes» of the validator (empty: publishable).
